canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

items.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b at 4.3 $μ$m. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

items.title: Measurement of the Neutrino Spectrum along the Galactic Plane with IceCube
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane using 10 years of neutrino-induced particle-shower data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In this Letter, we fit both the neutrino flux normalization and the spectral index, in multiple regions along the plane, independent of model expectations. The neutrino flux per solid angle in the inner Galactic region ($\vert l\vert< 30^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) is approximately five times higher than in the outer Galactic plane ($\vert l\vert>60^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) at $E_ν=5\mathrm{TeV}$. The spectral indices in the inner and outer region are $γ=2.76^{+0.18}_{-0.15}$ and $γ= 3.13^{+0.57}_{-0.37}$, respectively. Additionally, we compare the same region of Galactic emission measured in $\mathrm{TeV}$ gamma rays by LHAASO ($15^{\circ}<l<125^{\circ}$) to neutrinos, and conclude that the measurements are compatible within uncertainties, under the assumption of hadronic gamma-ray production.

items.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

items.title: Dark-Matter-Induced Nuclear Deexcitation at the Short-Baseline Near Detector with Ab Initio Nuclear Theory
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing localized low-energy “blip” signatures in a liquid argon time projection chamber. We perform state-of-the-art nuclear calculations, including all relevant argon excited states with energies up to 18 MeV, to provide reliable predictions for these signals. After accounting for relevant backgrounds, we find that SBND can probe previously unexplored regions of parameter space for light dark matter.

items.title: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak. Our results lend further support to a physical picture in which high-energy cosmic rays are predominantly supplied by local sources, whereas low-energy cosmic rays arise mainly from the collective contribution of sources in other regions of the Galaxy. We also calculate the neutrino spectra of these sources, providing theoretical predictions for future tests of the model through observations of point-source and diffuse neutrino emission.

items.title: A possible signature of neutrino spin precession in the J-PARC muon $g-2$ experiment
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We examine a possible signature of the neutrino angular-momentum contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly measurement in the J-PARC E34 experiment. In previous papers we argued that the angular momentum carried by the unobserved neutrino pair may leave an uncertainty in the anomaly inferred from the time modulation of detected positrons. At Fermilab the highly relativistic muons make the forward-emission approximation suitable for this estimate. The lower muon momentum at J-PARC requires the decay kinematics to be treated explicitly. We integrate the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the positron energy distribution and asymmetry derived from the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, and the same event-counting weight $N(E)A(E)$ is employed for both experiments. For positron energies between $1.5$ and $2.9$ GeV at Fermilab and between $200$ and $275$ MeV at J-PARC, the proposed correction is smaller at J-PARC by $0.415\pm0.176$ ppm, when the most optimistic E34 precision is assumed. The expected difference amounts to $2.36$ standard deviations if the future measurement is centred on this value. The calculation thus identifies an experimental comparison which may test the proposed effect independently of the hadronic contribution to the Standard Model prediction. We also examine the possibility of testing the effect by comparing measurements at two different muon momenta. With a fixed positron energy threshold of 200 MeV, the maximum sensitivity is obtained at a muon beam energy of 245 MeV. The predicted difference relative to the nominal J-PARC configuration has significance of $4.88σ$ for the most optimistic experimental sensitivity.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims survive every protocol we test: segregated reward and punishment dopamine improves learning, and head-direction topography is required for a persistent bump. Others do not. In the mushroom body, the real Kenyon-cell output wiring beats a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but loses to it by 0.09 under P3 (95% CIs exclude zero; held-out runs confirm). The verdict is set by the share of alpha'beta' cells among active Kenyon cells, which P1 selects low; at the share implied by imaging (about 44%) the real-wiring model fails to learn, exposing a model inadequacy rather than a deficit of the fly's wiring. In flyvis, P1 penalises a mirrored connectome, which has a constructed solution within 0.07 (median) of the real error, more than a spatially shuffled one in 50 of 50 members; the ranking survives ten-fold longer retraining but depends on the checkpoint at fifty-fold. A credible structural claim needs matched optimisation, data-constrained physiology and a model that still works there.

items.title: Projected sensitivity of the ANUBUIS detector to tau-coupled Heavy Neutral Leptons
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) provide a minimal and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model neutrino sector, and are naturally long-lived for small mixing angles between SM neutrinos and HNLs. A previous ANUBIS study determined the projected sensitivity to a single Majorana HNL coupled exclusively to the electron or to the muon, corresponding to the BC6 and BC7 benchmark scenarios of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative. The present article extends that work to the complementary BC8 scenario, in which the HNL couples exclusively to the tau lepton. As the tau lepton is itself unstable and because charged-current HNL decay modes become available only above the kinematic tau lepton production threshold, the production, decay and event-selection characteristics of this scenario cannot be obtained by rescaling the electron- or muon-coupled results in flavour. The analysis is carried out end to end, from signal-sample generation through acceptance evaluation to sensitivity extraction, with the released SET-ANUBIS~v1.0.0 framework.

items.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)—a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody–drug conjugate—has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)—a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study ( n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population ( n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59–1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

items.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

items.title: Beam-beam effects on measurements at electron-positron colliders: LEP neutrino counting and Higgs factories
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Beam-beam electromagnetic interactions affect the luminosity, collision energy, polarization, and particle backgrounds relevant to precision measurements at electron-positron colliders. We investigate these effects using Fast $e^{\pm}e^{\pm}$ Beam and Luminosity (FeeBL), a new beam-beam simulation framework, and compare its predictions with published results from LEP and proposed future colliders. We reproduce the analytical field-integration calculations of LEP Bhabha scattering and identify an approximately 2% bias in previously published beam-deflection simulations. Applying the corresponding luminosity correction and a revised uncertainty assessment motivated by the observed agreement among the four LEP experiments yields ($N_ν= 2.9965 \pm 0.0040$), compared with the previously reported ($2.9963 \pm 0.0074$). The revised uncertainty is conditional on an assumed common rescaling of experiment specific uncertainties and motivates further investigation of the original uncertainty budgets. We identify and correct implementation errors in the modeling of Breit-Wheeler, Bethe-Heitler, and Landau-Lifshitz pair production, with implications for detector backgrounds at Higgs factories. Simulated beam depolarization and luminosity spectra are compared with existing ILC and HALHF predictions. Finally, we investigate collision energy monochromatization for direct Higgs production, obtaining sub-MeV collision energy peak widths in exploratory linear collider configurations at substantial luminosity cost, while finding significantly weaker narrowing for the FCC-ee configurations studied. We derive a rigid Gaussian beam overlap model and estimate that FCC-ee needs roughly 10 m of horizontal only dispersion to reach widths of $\approx1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

items.title: Reproducible quantum clustering for single-cell transcriptome atlases
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Current single-cell clustering pipelines discard most genes and can yield inconsistent clusters across random seeds. We introduce KQE-2, a training-free hybrid quantum-classical framework for reproducible whole-transcriptome clustering. KQE-2 maps cells into entanglement-free quantum states, enabling exact feature evaluation on classical hardware and direct checks on a quantum processor. Theoretically, we prove that removing entanglement is necessary and sufficient to bound single-qubit feature variance locally. Practically, while retraining scVI shifted 14% of cells and altered rare-type markers and drug targets, KQE-2 delivered identical biology across runs. On standard highly variable genes, the quantum encoding alone raised accuracy on a developing cortex from 0.61 to 0.79. KQE-2 scales to 11.4 million nuclei on one server, outperforming the compared methods on eight of ten complete atlases (and within the best method's run-to-run range on two), and leads on six even under standard downstream clustering.

items.title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Quantum-mechanical interaction potentials support localized bound states below the dissociation threshold or delocalized scattering states above it. Although bound states are energetically isolated, scattering states couple a quantum system to environmental modes, making dissipation and loss intrinsic to open systems. Bound states in the continuum are an exception, as destructive interference keeps them localized within the scattering continuum. Theory predicts that such states can arise through interference between two Feshbach resonances coupled to a common continuum. Here we form such an interference-stabilized state in ultracold collisions of 6 Li atoms by coherently coupling two tunable Feshbach resonances using Floquet engineering. At a critical parameter point, elastic and inelastic coupling to the continuum vanish, producing a molecular state above the dissociation threshold. Consequently, resonant scattering features disappear and the colliding atoms become effectively transparent to one another. Full coupled-channel calculations and a minimal non-Hermitian model quantitatively reproduce our observations and identify the state as a Friedrich–Wintgen bound state in the continuum. These results show how quantum interference can control openness in quantum matter and enable the engineering of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

items.title: Filamentary dynamics in fan-like structures in high-altitude lightning discharges
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present LOFAR radio telescope measurements revealing that high-altitude negative leaders (HANLs) exhibit behavior completely different from the current paradigm of negative leader propagation. Our data show that the fan at the tip of a propagating HANL is formed by filaments that behave like smoothly advancing negative leaders. These negative leader filaments appear to have moderate conductivity, remain thin (radius $\sim1$ m), grow continuously at $\sim10^5$ m/s over hundreds of meters, and emit VHF radiation persistently. The observations show that the filaments making up the fan in front of a propagating negative leader are not necessarily streamers, as commonly assumed. Previous work suggesting to observe streamers at the tips of negative leaders should be re-examined in light of these new findings

items.title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

items.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

items.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

items.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

items.title: Sequential realization of Quantum Instruments
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2262 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-10-2262 In adaptive quantum circuits classical results of mid-circuit measurements determine the upcoming gates. This allows POVMs, quantum channels or more generally quantum instruments to be implemented sequentially, so that fewer qubits need to be used at each of the $N$ measurement steps. In this paper, we mathematically describe these problems via adaptive sequence of instruments (ASI) and show how any instrument can be decomposed into it. Number of steps $N$ and number of ancillary qubits $n_A$ needed for actual implementation are crucial parameters of any such ASI. We show an achievable lower bound on the product $N.n_A$ and we determine in which situations this tradeoff is likely to be optimal. Contrary to common intuition we show that for quantum instruments which transform $n$ to $m(\gt n)$ qubits, there exist $N$-step ASI implementing them just with $(m-n)$ ancillary qubits, which are remeasured $(N-1)$ times and finally used as output qubits.

items.title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.

items.title: High-power X-Point Target divertor experiments on the TCV tokamak
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Stationary power exhaust in the X-Point Target (XPT) divertor configuration is investigated in high-power ($2.5\,\text{MW}$) TCV L-mode discharges, in which the Lengyel detachment scaling metric $P_{\text{SOL}}B_{0}/(R_{0}n_{e,\text{u}}^{2})$ lies in the range expected for reactors (SPARC, ITER, ARC). Compared with a conventional single-null (SN) divertor, the XPT improves power exhaust performance, reducing the peak outer target heat flux by 40--60\% and enabling divertor detachment with nitrogen seeding under conditions in which the SN cannot be detached. Detachment evolves asymmetrically across the multiple XPT outer strike points. The sensitivities of the peak target heat fluxes and impurity emission front positions to the X-point separation ($\text{d}R_{\text{u},X2}$) are characterized and found to decrease at higher nitrogen seeding levels. Field-reversal experiments reveal the critical role of $E\times B$ drifts inherent to the magnetic topology of the secondary X-point, which drive an unconventional redistribution of density and impurity radiation in the XPT divertor and thereby cause the asymmetries between the XPT outer strike points, largely confirming the expectations from recent SOLPS-ITER modelling. A framework for understanding the power exhaust physics of the XPT is presented, detailing the roles of SOL splitting, connection length peaking, $E\times B$ drifts, and vessel geometry. Together, these results establish an experimental physics basis for the XPT divertor as a potential power exhaust solution for tokamak reactors.

items.title: Background-free and laser-ionization minimized single-shot fs-EFISH in luminous pulsed plasmas
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: This work introduces spectrally tuned electric field induced second harmonic (t-EFISH) generation for substantially reducing or eliminating background plasma emission in single-shot, time-resolved, electric field measurements. The technique is demonstrated using a femtosecond 1240 nm pump and 620 nm signal detection to avoid spectral and temporal overlap with the early, intense onset of N2(C-B) emission in nanosecond atmospheric-pressure air spark discharges. This enhances signal-to-emission ratios pre- and post-breakdown, enables lower pump energies, suppresses detector saturation, and reduces the coefficient of variation in the electric field measurements by 8.5x. This strategy also provides a pathway for background-free measurements in other discharge environments with varying spectro-temporal emission characteristics. Moreover, the longer 1240 nm pump wavelength reduces multiphoton intrusiveness, directly improving measurement fidelity.

items.title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a fusion-driven malignancy, peaking in adolescence. Although EwS tumors are driven uniquely by EWS::FLI1 and related fusions, patient outcomes vary greatly. If and how tumor plasticity of EWS::FLI1-regulated transcriptional signatures contributes to disease progression is not known. To address this, we utilized a single-cell co-assay of RNA and chromatin accessibility (ATAC) sequencing to identify gene regulatory networks in EwS. By comprehensively characterizing regulatory elements across cell lines, we identified multiple unique modules of gene regulation. Differential usage and prevalence of these modules was evident across cell lines, associated with distinct epigenetic and transcriptomic signatures, and in specific cases, modifiable by exogenous TGF-β. When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks. Our findings demonstrate that multiple, co-existing transcriptional programs shape the phenotypic diversity of EwS and suggest that the balance between these networks may have important implications for clinical outcomes and targeted therapy development.

items.title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features—one that enhances and one that suppresses activity—around an elevated baseline firing rate. By combining neuronal recordings with functional digital twin models—deep learning-based predictive models of biological neurons—we were able to systematically identify each neuron’s preferred and non-preferred features. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. We show that this encoding strategy is conserved across species, present in both primary and lateral visual areas of mouse cortex. items.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

items.title: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes and mapping of host and bacteria remodelling of the intracellular niche
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Ritika Chatterjee, José Luis Marin-Rubio, Francesca Romana Cianfanelli, Andrew Michael Frey, Benjamin Bernard Armando Raymond, Abeer Dannoura, Camila Valenzuela, Meihan Meng, Tiaan Heunis, Mengchun Li, Frances Sidgwick, Jost Enninga, Andrew Filby, Matthias Trost Macrophages engulf pathogens into dynamic phagosomes, which many bacteria manipulate for survival. However, isolating pure pathogen-containing phagosomes remains challenging. Here, we developed a novel flow cytometry-based isolation and ultrasensitive proteomics approach to analyse phagosomal and bacterial proteomes from macrophages infected with wild-type (WT) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STM) or a ΔphoP mutant at 30 min and 4 hours post-infection. Our approach provides higher throughput, requires lower cell numbers and quantifies more proteins than previous techniques. Our data reveals key host-pathogen interactions, showing induction of PhoP-dependent virulence factors and novel putative proteins that shape STM’s intracellular niche. Moreover, our data indicates that bacteria-containing phagosomes recruit mitochondrial membrane for production of reactive oxygen species. These findings provide new insights into Salmonella ’s manipulation of phagosomal maturation and intracellular niche formation.

items.title: Vertebrate paired fins are specified by an ancient dorso-ventral patterning system
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Rebecca E. Dale, Silke Berger, Sara Alaei, Marcus C. Davis, Frank J. Tulenko, Peter D. Currie The origin of paired fins was a major event in early vertebrate history that fueled the adaptive radiation of the gnathostome clade. Evidence for the conservation of ancient regulatory systems between paired and median fins supports a model in which appendage-patterning mechanisms first evolved in the midline and were later redeployed to a new embryonic context, the flank. However, while paired fins and limbs are asymmetric along the dorsoventral (DV) axis, the equivalent axis does not exist in median fins, which are symmetric across the midline, raising questions of how DV patterning evolved. Here, we combine genetic tools in zebrafish with comparative expression analyses in representative ray-finned and cartilaginous fishes to show that a subset of limb DV patterning genes are expressed during median fin development. Using genetic lineage tracing of the canonical limb dorsalizing factor lmx1bb , we further demonstrate that, although lmx1bb -derived cells occupy distinct spatial domains across fin types, a subset of this lineage is fated to differentiate into fin ray osteoblasts in both paired and median fins. To test the potential conservation of regulatory modules across fin types, we generated a series of deletion mutants for two known lmx1b mouse limb enhancers, LARM1 and LARM2

items.abstract: by Xiaoqing Ru, Yansu Wang, Quan Zou, Mengting Niu Reliable generalization is essential for deploying drug–drug interaction (DDI) and drug–target interaction (DTI) models in drug discovery, pharmacovigilance, and clinical decision support. In pairwise prediction, test instances may still resemble training examples in molecular structure, sequence, or network context. items.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Emma E. Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, Ruian Ke The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid population growth. From early sequence data collected in the US and the UK between 2021 and mid-2022, we identified two features—genetic diversity and graph connectivity—that allow us to reliably estimate growth rates of newly emerged lineages. To test our model, we used data collected from mid-2022 to end-2024 and accurately inferred the growth rates of lineages that appeared during this period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for data collected in 2023 when the sequencing efforts were relatively high (thousands of sequences per day) in the US and the UK, our model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. items.title: County-level spatial heterogeneity and environmental correlates of human echinococcosis in Xizang, China
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (verified on article pages; occasional CC0)
items.abstract: by Jiajia Ai, Lamu Ciren, Quzhen Gongsang, Lamu Suolang, Xiaoyao Ji, Jiakun Wang, Yangjin Baima, Zhaohui Luo, Zhuoma Bianba Background Human echinococcosis remains a major zoonosis in Xizang, China, where marked climatic, topographic and landscape gradients may be associated with spatial variation in disease prevalence. We investigated county-level spatial patterns of overall human echinococcosis, cystic echinococcosis (CE) and alveolar echinococcosis (AE), and their environmental associations. Methods Surveillance data from 74 counties during 2019–2023 were analysed. Because usable surveillance data were unavailable for 32 counties in 2022, that year was excluded from the spatial and generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) analyses. Global and local Moran’s I assessed spatial autocorrelation and clustering. items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2270 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-10-2270 Many-body ground state preparation is an important subroutine used in the simulation of physical systems. In this paper, we introduce a flexible and efficient framework for obtaining a state preparation circuit for a large class of many-body ground states. We introduce polynomial-time classical algorithms that take reduced density matrices over $\mathcal{O}(1)$-sized balls as inputs, and output a circuit that prepares the global state. We introduce algorithms applicable to (i) short-range entangled states (e.g., states prepared by shallow quantum circuits in any number of dimensions, and more generally, invertible states) and (ii) long-range entangled ground states (e.g., the toric code on a disk). Both algorithms can provably find a circuit whose depth is asymptotically optimal. Our approach uses a variant of the quantum Markov chain condition that remains robust against constant-depth circuits. The robustness of this condition makes our method applicable to a large class of states, whilst ensuring a classically tractable optimization landscape.

items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2269 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-10-2269 We introduce a general framework for the analysis of non-Gaussian entanglement in bosonic states of finite stellar rank. The central result is the full characterization of their entanglement structure through the atomic decomposition of their stellar polynomial and its associated structural graph, whose connected components determine the mode-intrinsic entanglement content of the state and all partitions compatible with passive separability. An essential ingredient in this construction is the concept of essential variables, which identify the minimal number of effective modes involved in a core state, in direct correspondence with the symplectic rank. This reduction provides the foundation for decomposing stellar polynomials into atomic factors and for revealing the underlying entanglement structure. Building on this, we derive complete separability criteria for two-mode states, expressed through hyperplane decompositions of zero sets, and for stellar-rank-2 states across an arbitrary number of modes. Applications to several example states illustrate how the method isolates genuinely non-Gaussian resources and quantifies preparation complexity.

items.title: Detection of local recombination and mutation hotspots in bacterial genomes using neural posterior estimation
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Motivation: Recombination and mutation rates in bacteria vary along the genome, and regions of elevated rate (hotspots) often reflect selection on specific genes. Detecting them is difficult because the two processes leave overlapping signals in sequence data, clonal relationships act as a confounder, and inference must scale to whole genomes. Existing methods assume a constant mutation rate and/or rely on a small set of summary statistics. Results: We present a simulation-based framework that infers gene-specific recombination and mutation rates under a well-specified model of bacterial recombination. Neural posterior estimation (NPE) is trained on simulations conditioned on a fixed clonal genealogy, using a wide range of summary statistics. Gene length is also used as both a parameter and an observed statistic, so that the model learns about its effect on other statistics and thus becomes applicable across different gene lengths. To identify hotspots, we introduce a circular posterior-propagated Difference-of-Gaussians detector that contrasts local and regional smoothers of the posterior log rates, carrying NPE uncertainty into hotspot probabilities. On simulated data, the method recovers the true rates, with credible intervals that narrow as gene length increases. We also apply the new methodology to three real datasets in Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli to showcase its usefulness in a range of situations. Availability and implementation: The Python implementation is freely available from https://github.com/haochu-liu/bacnpe.

items.title: Midbrain somatostatin-expressing cells control pain-suppression during defensive states
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST + vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST + vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST + vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST + vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.

items.title: OriDynamics: Towards a World Model for Biomolecular Dynamics
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Biomolecular recognition and regulation depend on atomic interactions that change as molecular partners fluctuate and adopt alternative conformations. Modeling these processes requires ensembles that capture both conformational diversity and coordinated atomic fluctuations between interacting molecules. Here we present OriDynamics, a unified framework for all-atom ensemble generation across protein monomers and complexes with small molecules or protein partners. OriDynamics introduces a latent ensemble decomposition that couples broad conformational exploration in a compact structural latent space with local all-atom sampling around generated proposals. Ensemble-level supervision constrains mean positions, fluctuation amplitudes and joint coordinate covariance to capture coordinated atomic variability within and between molecular partners. Across benchmarks of proteins and their complexes, OriDynamics demonstrates superior overall performance in conformational coverage, atomic fluctuation fidelity and interaction geometry compared with leading baselines. Application studies further demonstrate recovery of alternative functional conformations and partner-dependent changes in conformational ensembles alongside sampling of configurations associated with ligand dissociation. These capabilities provide a foundation for a biomolecular world model that represents accessible molecular states and their dependence on interaction context.

items.title: Virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight performance are mediated by the octopamine pathway
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the ‘fight-or-flight’ response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) – an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. Transcriptome analyses indicated that SBV infections, and DWV infection with OA treatment, activated honey bee metabolic pathways, and that SBV-infected bees had greater expression of genes involved in OA synthesis, unless treated with OA. items.title: Symmetry-Induced Conservation Laws, Three-Channel Attribution, and Solid-Phase Recycling in Prebiotic Enantiomeric Excess Amplification
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Enantiomeric excess ($\mathrm{ee}$) is the primary observable used to quantify chiral amplification across prebiotic chemistry, asymmetric autocatalysis, and multiphase crystallization. Because $\mathrm{ee} = Δ/ M$ is the ratio of net chiral excess $Δ= L - D$ to total chiral mass $M = L + D$, identical increases in $\mathrm{ee}$ can arise either by generating net chiral excess through parity-breaking reactions or by depleting total chiral mass through symmetric phase or oligomer partitioning. Here we establish a pathwise conservation law and a model-free three-channel attribution identity for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric reaction networks. In any closed network without autocatalytic feedback or epimerization, net chiral excess is conserved along every stochastic trajectory ($Δ(t) = Δ(0)$), locking liquid-phase amplification to cumulative mass loss ($\mathrm{ee}_f = \mathrm{ee}_0 M_0 / M_f$). Re-analyzing seven experimental systems shows that standalone phase removal (Channel R) loses $91.7\%$--$98.9\%$ of chiral solute into racemic sediment in closed batches and washes out under open racemic inflow. Coupling eutectic partitioning (Channel R) with solid/solution racemization recycling (Channel B) converts the precipitated solid into homochiral product ($96.5\%$ recoverable homochiral crystal mass at $96.5\%$ total and $100.0\%$ solid $\mathrm{ee}$), whereas coupling evaporative concentration with liquid-phase autocatalysis crosses the open-flow bifurcation threshold against continuous racemic dilution ($81.9\%$ homochiral yield at $92.9\%$ active chiral $\mathrm{ee}$). We further establish non-crossing parity invariants for dual-monomer networks, derive a closed-form wet--dry amplification law, and resolve a one-dimensional identifiability ridge in chiral mineral adsorption via antipodal crystal-pair protocols.

items.title: Large inversions in Lake Malawi cichlids are associated with habitat, lineage, and sex determination
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. items.title: Simple methods to acutely measure multiple timing metrics among the sexual repertoire of male Drosophila
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.

items.title: Spatial confinement induces oscillatory migration of epidermal keratinocytes and forms a three-compartment epithelial structure with epithelial–mesenchymal transition dynamics
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). We established an experimental system that reproduces a three-compartment epithelial structure comprising the original epithelium, its EMT state, and its MET state. Keratinocytes (KCs), skin epithelial cells, placed on a microporous membrane, migrated through 3.0 µm or larger micropores. The 3.0-µm-pored membrane induced an epithelial structure with three distinct states: stratified KCs above the membrane, KCs showing EMT within the micropores, and a new stratified epithelium under the membrane. The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.

items.title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Many bacteria form spores to endure unfavorable conditions. While Firmicutes generate endospores through cell division, sporulation in non-Firmicutes remains less understood. The Gram-negative bacterium Myxococcus xanthus undergoes sporulation through two distinct mechanisms: rapid sporulation triggered by chemical induction and slow sporulation driven by starvation, both occurring independently of cell division. Instead, these processes depend on the complete degradation of the peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall by two lytic transglycosylases (LTGs), LtgA and LtgB. Remarkably, LtgB programs the pace of PG degradation by LtgA during rapid sporulation, ensuring a controlled process that prevents abrupt PG breakdown and the formation of non-resistant pseudospores. In addition to regulation between LTGs, PG degradation is also influenced by its synthesis; cells exhibiting increased muropeptide production often circumvent sporulation. These findings not only reveal novel mechanisms of bacterial sporulation but also shed light on the regulatory network governing PG dynamics.

items.title: Can the exposome help solve the alcohol and cancer mystery?
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Vasilis Vasiliou, Arthur Stem, David C. Thompson Alcohol consumption is a preventable driver of many cancers, yet a central biological question remains unresolved: by what mechanisms does ethanol promote malignancy? We propose that alcohol in the context of the exposome (i.e., the network of chemical, biological, and social determinants that interact with ethanol across the life span) provides a unifying framework for understanding alcohol-related carcinogenesis. Viewed through the lens of the exposome, alcohol is not only as a direct carcinogen but also as a systemic amplifier of environmental risk acting across multiple levels of biological organization, from molecular damage to whole-body physiology. This reframing has important implications for mechanistic research, precision prevention, and public-health policy.

items.title: Ten simple rules for a department chair
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Lubomir Tomaska Department chairs occupy a pivotal position in the university. Teaching, research, graduate education, and much of the academic community's professional and administrative activity are organized at the departmental level. Yet, despite the importance of the position and the considerable challenges it entails, many scientists assume the role with little or no formal preparation for academic leadership. This paper is intended as a practical primer rather than a comprehensive guide to academic leadership. The proposed rules provide a framework that prospective and current department chairs can adapt to their own institutional circumstances, experience, and leadership style.

items.title: A computational framework to model cartilage degeneration induced by mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation in post-traumatic osteoarthritis
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Moustafa Hamada, Atte S. A. Eskelinen, Joonas P. Kosonen, Sanna Hakonen, Cristina Florea, Alan J. Grodzinsky, Rami K. Korhonen, Petri Tanska Knee joint injury is a major risk factor for post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), often associated with early cartilage degeneration. Mechanical overloading and cytokine-driven inflammation are key drivers of this process, yet the underlying mechanisms and their distinct temporal and spatial contributions to cartilage degradation remain unclear. Here, we present a mechanobiological finite element framework that simulates cartilage degradation through cell-mediated proteolytic activity triggered by injurious loading-driven mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation. The model reproduces experimentally observed depth-dependent loss of collagen and aggrecan, with mechanoinflammation inducing a transient response and cytokine-driven inflammation sustaining prolonged matrix degradation. Sensitivity analysis further shows that mechanoinflammation-driven degradation is governed mainly by protease production per cell, whereas cytokine-driven degradation is more sensitive to the rate of cellular stimulation. Together, this framework provides a mechanistic basis to study proteolytic cartilage degeneration and supports future in silico evaluation of therapeutic strategies aimed at mitigating cartilage degradation in PTOA.

While interviews and focus groups are widely used, these methods are often time‑limited and project‑specific. Global health roundtables offer a complementary approach, providing a flexible and long-term platform for engaging diverse stakeholders—including researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and community representatives—in collective dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaboration. items.abstract: by Il Memming Park, Jonathan W. Pillow The efficient coding hypothesis, which proposes that neurons are optimized to maximize information about the environment, has provided a guiding theoretical framework for sensory and systems neuroscience. More recently, a theory known as the Bayesian Brain hypothesis has focused on the brain’s ability to integrate sensory and prior sources of information in order to perform Bayesian inference. Although pieces of a connection between these two hypotheses have appeared in prior work, a general formulation that treats the optimality criterion as an arbitrary functional of the posterior distribution – and thereby admits both information-based and other objectives within a single framework – has remained largely implicit.
